evidence: The FBP method is analysed in section 3 and the motivation for and details of discretizing the density at every iteration are described in section 4. The measure of the similarity of the sinograms is calculated by counting the percentage of points in s_i and sE that have converged to within a specified percentage accuracy. The mass density calculated from sE is shown in figure 2(c). The FBP method is expressed mathematically in equation (6), r(x,y)=R−1s(p,θ)=B[F−1_1 [|p|F1(s(p,θ))]] (6) where the operators B, F1 and F−1_1 are the backprojection, the one-dimensional Fourier and the one-dimensional inverse-Fourier transforms respectively. The FBP method is used with the Shepp–Logan filter at full bandwidth. Using this reconstruction method with the experimental sinogram sE provided the reference reconstruction rE. The FBP method is a discrete version of the inverse Radon transform, noise was generated and care had to be taken in identifying the zero voxels of rE.
